texts: bad: the consequent's "a station near the Sunken Cove" is lifted out of the condition — the parse asserts outright that such a station exists and sits near the cove, and it fixes one and the same station as the requester for every draining, neither of which your sentence claims; separately, "at the Sunken Cove" attaches to the lantern rather than to the draining, so the rule keys on where the lantern sits. Rewrite as: "Whenever a wraith drains a Sunken Cove lantern, the station near the Sunken Cove requests feather rations from the Council." — the definite "the station" makes the one standing station the stated reading, so asserting it is licensed, and "a Sunken Cove lantern" ties the cove to the lantern with no attachment ambiguity left.

good. it becomes a fireable rule that triggers on any station's report, treats "drained" as a property of the lantern rather than a second event, and hands that same reporting station to the Council's prioritizing — nothing lost.
